author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Bob vs QTGMC Deinterlacing | Field Rendering PlayStation 2
summary: A side-by-side comparison of bob and QTGMC deinterlacing on PlayStation 2 footage makes motion and combing tradeoffs visible across five games.
searchKeywords: Bob vs QTGMC Deinterlacing | Field Rendering PlayStation 2

blocks.text: The clip compares two ways of turning interlaced PS2 output into progressive frames. It names Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex, Ridge Racer V, Tekken 4, Rez and Dead or Alive 2, giving several kinds of motion to examine rather than one favorable still frame. Bob keeps each field as a moment in time but can emphasize vertical shimmer. QTGMC is a more elaborate reconstruction path whose processing can change the appearance of fine detail and motion.

This is a video-processing comparison of captured console material, not a benchmark of an emulator renderer. Display scaling, source capture and online compression also affect what a viewer sees. Pause at moving edges, text and fine lines, then compare the same timestamp rather than judging by a thumbnail. An emulator's live deinterlacing settings may use different algorithms or input assumptions, so the clip is most useful for learning what artifacts to look for when testing PS2 output.
